standard_prerequisites: The Godel sentence G_T for an axiomatizable theory T extending Q, as constructed in the unit's incompleteness section.
Omega-consistency of T: T does not prove both an existential statement and the negation of each numeral instance of its matrix.
The two sibling results proved in the same unit: a consistent T does not derive G_T, and an omega-consistent T does not derive the negation of G_T.

The one-line observation that omega-consistency implies consistency: an inconsistent theory derives every numeral instance of any formula together with the negated existential, so it is omega-inconsistent.
core_obligations: Compose the two sibling lemmas into the incompleteness conclusion: omega-consistency implies consistency, so the first sibling lemma applies and T does not derive G_T; the second sibling lemma gives that T does not derive the negation of G_T; a theory deriving neither a sentence nor its negation is incomplete.
proof_roadmap: Apply omega-consistency implies consistency to license the first sibling lemma.
Apply the second sibling lemma verbatim and conclude incompleteness by the definition of completeness for T.
difficulty_reason: A two-lemma composition that is the capstone of the unit's first incompleteness chain; the substantive step is recognizing that omega-consistency implies consistency, which licenses the consistency-only lemma, plus matching the two non-derivability results to the definition of incompleteness.
